tweet_summary: A men's-rights advocacy account ('NCM India') visits Kirti Nagar Police Station demanding the arrest of activist Jasmeet Kaur Arora, who was videoed slapping a security guard with a slipper outside the station. The tweet frames her as the 'Dog Woman who abused and assaulted' the guard.
why_note_decision: Both facts the original note adds are essentially confirmed by Indian news reports (Sunday Guardian, India TV, Tribune, Statesman, NewsX): guard Vinod Paswan attacked a stray dog with an iron rod, dog later died, FIRs were filed against both the guard (BNS 325 + PCA Act) and Jasmeet (BNS 115(1), 126). However the tweet itself is an advocacy/opinion post calling for arrest and saying 'violence cannot be tolerated' — both true statements. It does not deny the dog incident. The note injects context the tweet author may dispute but isn't lying about. This is opinion/framing territory: both sides have legitimate grievances and police actions are documented. A Community Note arguing the assault was justified by alleged prior animal cruelty steps into opinion-speculation territory.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet is an advocacy post calling for arrest after a video of an assault; both parties have FIRs and both narratives (guard killed dog vs guard chased biting dog) are reported. A note that justifies the assault as a response to the dog killing is opinion/speculation and crosses into argumentative-or-biased territory. A note that merely says 'guard allegedly killed dog' is partial truth that takes one side. Best response: no note.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The woman in the video is animal activist Jasmeet Kaur Arora. She slapped the security guard after he had allegedly beaten a stray dog to death with a stick that morning. Police officers were present watching. https://www.news18.com/amp/viral/watch-delhi-woman-slaps-guard-with-chappal-outside-police-station-after-he-allegedly-kills-stray-dog-10083874.html https://hindustanherald.in/delhi-guard-kills-stray-dog-kirti-nagar/
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: noteNotNeeded / argumentative — adds context that takes one side of a disputed incident with FIRs against both parties; the tweet is opinion/advocacy, not factual misinformation.

fact_check.claim_verdict: Underlying events are real and accurately reported by both sides. Note's added context is partially correct (guard accused; dog died; police present) but the tweet's framing is opinion/advocacy, not falsifiable misinformation.
fact_check.notes: Both FIRs filed; the assault happened May 9 outside the police station, dog died after May 7 incident. Tweet is advocacy demanding arrest after a real video assault.

importance.lens_rationale: Local Delhi incident with animal-welfare angle; modest EA/animal-welfare relevance but no major global stakes.
